function: above_phy, p. 2 and p. 8: DDQN learns aerial-user association to terrestrial base stations or LEO satellites and DDPG learns aerial-user trajectories for MEC task offloading; resource allocation uses convex optimization.
notes: Title on p. 1 matches the DOI. The learned components act above the physical layer: p. 2: "we employ double deep Q-learning (DDQN) and deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithms to solve the association and trajectory optimization problems, respectively. Finally, the task allocation problem and resource allocation problems are tackled by using the convex optimization technique." p. 8: "we employ DDQN and DDPG methods to address the association and trajectory optimization problems, respectively." User association, UAV trajectory, and task offloading decisions are listed under above_phy. The satellite/aerial exception does not apply because no physical-layer decision is learned: TBS bandwidth and computing allocation are solved with CVXPY (p. 11: "we can solve (51) by using CVXPY solver and obtain the bandwidth and computing resource allocation values"), the AUE-to-LEO bandwidth is fixed at 50 MHz (p. 12), and the transmit powers are fixed parameters (p. 11, Table II: pu, pn = 5 W, 0.1 W) that are not variables of problem (34) (p. 7). Code no_learning was not chosen because DRL is the core method; it simply acts above the physical layer. The objective is total energy of AUEs, TUEs, and LEO satellites in an ITNT-MEC system (p. 1).
